summary: Private deploy: split-horizon DNS returns internal A for control plane causing artifact fetches to hit unreachable private IP
description: Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent model artifact fetch failures from their private deployment in prod/us-east-1. Symptoms seen as repeated timeouts and TLS handshake errors when the control plane attempts to pull model artifacts. Impact: model loads fail for a subset of nodes causing degraded capacity and 503 responses to tenant requests. Environment: Private deployment using VPC peering to connect customer VPCs to Redwood control plane endpoints via a TGW. Customer operates an on-prem resolver chain and uses conditional forwarders for redwood endpoints.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) On a worker node inside the customer's VPC, run: curl -v https://control-plane.redwood.internal/healthz
2) Attempt to pull model artifact via the platform agent: /usr/local/bin/redwood-agent fetch --model redwood/gpt-large-v1
3) Observe connection failures only from nodes that resolve control-plane.redwood.internal to 10.200.0.5 (customer-private IP)
4) Switch resolver to 9.9.9.9 (public) and repeat; artifact fetch succeeds consistently.
logs:
[2026-03-10T09:12:03Z] agent.fetch: GET https://control-plane.redwood.internal/v1/artifacts/redwood/gpt-large-v1 -> dial tcp 10.200.0.5:443: connect: network is unreachable
[2026-03-10T09:12:06Z] agent.tls: TLS handshake error: remote error: tls: handshake failure (server returned unexpected certificate name)
[2026-03-10T09:12:06Z] control-plane: request_id=abc123 fetch timeout after 15s
Resolver output (node-a): control-plane.redwood.internal. 300 IN A 10.200.0.5
Resolver output (public test): control-plane.redwood.internal. 300 IN A 52.45.112.11
comments: 2026-03-10 10:02 - Aisha Kumar (Support): Initial triage - customer shows failing artifact downloads, appears DNS-related based on early logs.
2026-03-10 11:10 - Marco Lin (SRE): Ran traceroute from affected node; next hop to 10.200.0.5 goes to blackhole - no route to TGW attachment for customer's secondary CIDR.
2026-03-10 14:35 - FinLedger (Customer): We confirmed our internal resolver returns 10.200.0.5 for control-plane endpoints due to legacy conditional forwarder pointing to an on-prem appliance.

2026-03-11 09:12 - Aisha Kumar (Support): Applied temporary mitigation - advised customer to add conditional forwarder to RDNS that resolves control-plane.redwood.internal to public IPs via public forwarder. Artifact pulls succeeded after change.

2026-03-12 15:40 - Marco Lin (SRE): Observed intermittent reappearances when resolver cache TTL expired. Created route table update request with customer to ensure TGW route for 10.200.0.0/20 is propagated to the right VPC attachment.
2026-03-13 08:05 - Customer: Confirmed update to route table propagated; no new failures observed in 24h.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: split-horizon DNS combined with incomplete TGW route propagation caused the control plane A-record to resolve to a private on-prem IP (10.200.0.5) for some nodes. When agent attempted TLS to 10.200.0.5 the path was unreachable (no route via TGW/VPC peering) causing dial-level errors. Also observed certificate name mismatch when connection did succeed to the private IP (internal appliance terminating TLS with different CN). Evidence: dig from affected nodes showed A -> 10.200.0.5 while public dig returned Redwood public IP. Traceroute showed blackhole at TGW attachment that lacked route for the customer's secondary CIDR. Correlated with customer's recent network change: added a conditional forwarder and a new on-prem resolver that advertises a private range for control-plane hostnames.
resolution: Workaround (applied): Customer added a conditional forwarder for control-plane.redwood.internal pointing to a public resolver and temporarily increased TTL to flush incorrect records; artifact fetches succeeded. Longer-term fix actions agreed: 1) Customer will add explicit route propagation for 10.200.0.0/20 to their TGW attachment and remove the legacy conditional forwarder for Redwood hostnames. 2) Support updated runbook: add a DNS check step for split-horizon resolution during private deployment onboarding. 3) Engineering task created to improve agent diagnostics to surface resolved IP vs expected public IP and to fail-fast with clearer messaging (see PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2934). Follow-ups: Confirmed by customer on 2026-03-12 that route table change removed the blackhole; monitoring for 72h to close the ticket. Postmortem: update onboarding checklist and sample resolver config to prevent conditional forwarder leakage.
notes: Priority elevated because this impacts artifact fetch and can reduce serving capacity for the customer. Recommended outreach: Solutions Engineering to follow up with FinLedger on updated onboarding docs and confirm we can whitelist public control-plane FQDNs in their resolver policies.
